subject.title: [Bug]: Compaction fails with 'Thread group size (1024) exceeds maximum threads per threadgroup (896)'

question: Should failed overflow compaction for local OpenAI-compatible providers remain fail-closed, or should OpenClaw add a provider-agnostic degraded recovery path when the compaction model rejects summarization?
rationale: Current code intentionally blocks after recovery paths are exhausted, while the reporter’s desired behavior changes session liveness and may introduce new fallback or configuration surface.

options.title: Design Provider-Agnostic Recovery
options.body: Add a safe recovery path for compaction-provider failures, such as alternate compaction routing, visible non-reset recovery, or clearer session rollover, without starting with an MLX-specific knob.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed Semantics
options.body: Keep blocked liveness as the safe default and improve diagnostics/docs so operators can switch compaction models or provider params themselves.

options.title: Add MLX-Specific Tuning
options.body: Introduce a dedicated compaction/provider parameter only after maintainers confirm MLX exposes a stable request field that existing `extra_body` cannot cover.

recommendation.title: Design Provider-Agnostic Recovery
recommendation.body: Add a safe recovery path for compaction-provider failures, such as alternate compaction routing, visible non-reset recovery, or clearer session rollover, without starting with an MLX-specific knob.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on overflow recovery budgeting makes this the closest current-main ownership trail for the failed-compaction recovery decision.
